.._comment_skip: release-please targets main and still must NOT cut the tag, for a reason that changed on 2026-08-30 while the setting did not. It used to be that it ran against dev and a tag there would be a false claim. Now it is that the sibling job in the same workflow builds the wheel and sdist and attaches them, and release-please does neither: letting it cut the release would produce a tag with no artifacts. release-please proposes the version and writes CHANGELOG.md; the arrival of that version on main is what gets tagged. Skipping the release phase also skips its bookkeeping: a shipped release PR is recognised by its `autorelease: tagged` label, not by the tag, and while a merged PR still wears `autorelease: pending` every run aborts before proposing the next version. v0.2.0's PR froze the pipeline that way for three days, so release.yml's tag step now does the label swap itself.
.._comment_extra_files: CITATION.cff carries the same version and nothing was updating it, so it would have drifted at the first release. tests/test_version_agreement.py checks the result rather than trusting this list, because an updater that silently matches nothing is this repository's most familiar failure.
